## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The retry loop works and its tests cover every branch, but its cap is 10 attempts. The project policy file listed in the manifest (`AGENTS.md`, read as the review criterion) says retry helpers under app/ "must cap attempts at 5". This PR's `AGENTS.md` hunk raises that cap to 10. The only reason given is that "the upstream now sheds load itself", and nothing in the repository supports that, so I reviewed against the cap of 5.

## Critical
- app/net.py:13 — correctness — `fetch_with_retry` defaults to `attempts=10`, and the guard at app/net.py:19 (`if not 1 <= attempts <= 10`) accepts up to 10. A caller using the default against a down upstream makes 10 `fetch` calls. Each call can wait up to its 10 s timeout, and there are 9 × 0.5 s sleeps between them. The policy caps these helpers at 5 attempts. Could you set the default and upper bound to 5 (`attempts=5`, `1 <= attempts <= 5`, with the matching docstring and `ValueError` message)? You would also need to update `test_fetch_with_retry_default_attempt_count` (tests/test_net.py:53) and the out-of-range values in tests/test_net.py:95 to `(0, 6)`. — Against a down upstream, each call can keep hitting it for roughly 104 s instead of about 52 s at 5 attempts. The policy says unbounded retries have already caused outages in exactly this situation.

## Strengths
- Retries catch only `OSError`, so other errors propagate immediately. After the last attempt fails, the original exception is re-raised with a bare `raise`, so callers see the real error.
- Tests read in full cover all three outcomes: success after failures (tests/test_net.py:23), running out of attempts (tests/test_net.py:56) and no sleep on a single attempt (tests/test_net.py:74). They also check both ends of the allowed range (default of 10 at tests/test_net.py:38; values 0 and 11 at tests/test_net.py:94).
